title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-03-18
content:
Summary:
- Focus this week: kernel selection and fusion work (small-model kernels), KV cache correctness and eviction, continuous batching tunings and backpressure adjustments.
- Primary goal: stabilize kernel fallback path + reduce p99 gen latency for long-context workloads while keeping stable tail latencies under load.

Highlights:
- Kernel work: landed fused matmul+gelu path for 8-bit kernels on A100 and L4; microbenchmarks show ~9% throughput improvement for short sequences (<512) and ~5% reduction in p99 for 1k-2k tokens. (PRs: #832, #839)
- KV cache: fixed a correctness edge-case for cache invalidation when model variant rollouts overlap (SR-1245). Added a light-weight eviction heuristic that reduces memory churn for chat workloads by ~12%.
- Batching: adjusted continuous batching aggressiveness; introduced adaptive max-batch-size per queue and a soft latency SLO to cap batch windows under high concurrency which reduced 95th percentile latency spikes during traffic spikes.

Kernel work (details):
- PR #832: fused matmul + gelu for int8 path. Implementation notes: added a small fusion dispatcher in kernel_selector that picks fused kernels when sequence_length <= 512 and batch_size >= 4. Falls back to non-fused path when memory pressure high.
  - Microbench: seq=256, batch=8, model=gpt-medium-7B-quant -> +9% throughput, p99 -6ms.
  - TODO: add more cross-platform microbench (L4 vs A100) and add telemetry counters for fallback reasons.
- PR #839: safe-kernel-fallback tests + CI perf job. Adds deterministic seeds for microbench harness and a stress test that runs fused -> fallback -> fused cycles to catch stateful kernel regressions.
- Open: need to finalize kernel ABI for grouped-attention fused kernels (design doc on Confluence). Liam to drive standardization with release-engineering.

KV cache work (details):
- Bug fix: Race when rolling out KV cache format v2 -> v3. Root cause was stale pointer retention in async GC path. Fix landed (SR-1245) and validated in staging with synthetic chat traces.
- Eviction heuristic: implemented LRU-ish hybrid that favors preserving recent prefixes for multi-turn chat. Results: memory footprint down ~12% on customer X trace.
- Metrics added: kv_cache.evictions_total, kv_cache.eviction_reason (memory_pressure|rollout), kv_cache.hits/misses per-route.
- Outstanding: need to add KV cache telemetry to per-route dashboard (console team). Filed SR-1302 to track.

Batching and scheduling:
- Reduced batch window default from 8ms to 6ms for low-latency tier; added adaptive window doubling under high throughput to reduce per-token compute.
- Introduced per-worker soft batch_size cap driven by estimated kv-cache hit-rate. Rationale: high cache hit-rate -> larger batches are beneficial because generation cost amortizes; low hit-rate -> favor smaller batches for latency.
- Backpressure: tuned queue length watermark to start shedding work to best-effort pool earlier to avoid head-of-line blocking. This reduced p99 spikes under sudden burst by ~20%.

Standup / daily notes (Mon-Fri):
- Mon: kernel PR #832 review, initial fused dispatcher landed. Discovered minor mem leak in int8 path; added sanitizer test.
- Tue: KV race repro on staging; bisected to async GC path, patch landed. Batch window experiment started (A/B).
- Wed: load test with chat-sim trace: observed p99 improvements but ~1% error increase for long tails -> traced to fallback path thrash. Added stabilization delay (200ms) to avoid rapid kernel toggles.
- Thu: CI perf jobs flaked due to noise on L4 nightly; increased samples and adjusted gating thresholds.
- Fri: retro + planning; agreed next week to prioritize telemetry and rollout plan for fused kernels.

Metrics / quick numbers (test cluster, stable commit):
- baseline -> current: 7% average throughput increase for short sequences, 8% p99 latency reduction for seq 1k-2k in staging cluster (L4 pool).
- KV cache: hit rate steady at ~78% for chat workload A, memory use down 12% after eviction heuristic.
- Batching: avg batch size up 1.3x during high-concurrency tests, p99 spikes down ~20% with new backpressure.

Action items / todos:
- Ava: add fallback telemetry counters to kernel_selector and expose in console (GH #846).
- Liam: finalize grouped-attention kernel ABI and update Confluence design doc.
- Sofia: wire kv_cache metrics into per-route dashboard and ensure retention policy meets SLOs (SR-1302).
- Noah: extend CI perf job to include mixed-seq-length traces and deterministic runs; reduce flakiness.
- Team: schedule canary rollout for fused kernels to 10% of L4 pool next Tue; monitor kv cache evictions and error rates closely.

Blockers / risks:
- Kernel fallback oscillation under noisy telemetry -> mitigated with stabilization delay but needs more robust signal to avoid SLO regressions.
- CI perf noise on L4 makes gating conservative; may slow rollout. Discuss with release-eng to get access to quieter perf infra.
- One remaining correctness edge-case: token-level cache invalidation when using model variants with different key ordering. Need a small compatibility shim; Noah to prototype.

Meetings / decisions:
- Thu sync: agreed to add a soft stabilization window before switching kernels (200ms).
- Ops sync: canary plan approved — 10% traffic, 48h hold, automatic rollback on error rate > 0.5% absolute.

Next week (priorities):
1) Telemetry: implement kernel fallback reasons metric + expose in Console.
2) Rollout: execute 10% canary for fused kernels on L4 pool; monitor.
3) KV: finish compatibility shim for variant ordering and add unit tests.
4) Batching: run full mixed-workload perf suite and finalize default batch window setting per tier.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we keep the fused kernel enabled by default for dedicated pools? (Pros: perf wins; Cons: risk of small correctness regressions visible to customers). Proposal: default off for Dedicated until canary completes, default on for Hosted low-latency tier behind feature flag.
- Should eviction heuristic be per-route configurable? (Sofia thinks yes for enterprise chat customers). Need product input on UI surface and defaults.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider per-model kernel profiles persisted in model-catalog so kernel_selector can make faster decisions without expensive microbench at startup.
- Explore light-weight per-request hints from the agent layer (e.g., expected response length) to tune batching faster.
